messages.subject: same N-mixture model, different output?
parts:
Dear all,

i am relatively new to Hierarchical Modelling and adopted the Binomial Mix-Mod with overdispersion in abundance and detection from Kéry & Schaub (2012) for a bird species from 4 sites and 4 years with 5 reps each. I want to include detection covariates and therefore rewrote the part:
lp[i,j,k]  ~ dnorm(beta[k], tau.p) into
lp[i,j,k]  <-   beta[k] + delta[i,j,k] now defining beta[k] and the covariate betas (1&2) in the priors like this:
# Priors
for (k in 1:4){
    alpha.lam[k] ~ dnorm(0, 0.1)
    beta[k] ~ dnorm(0, 0.1)
}
beta1 ~ dnorm(0,0.2) # betas for covariate
beta2 ~ dnorm(0,0.2)
The models run smoothly both, with and without detection covariates and model fit is just fine with fit/fit.new ~ 1. However, i am wondering about the different output from the null models. I expected posteriors to be the same or at least close together but e.g. deviance and DIC are 176; 305  in the "book"-model and 146; 278 in the modified model. Did i miss something during model modification?
I also wondered about the relatively broad confidence intervals when building effect plots for example for rainfall sum (rsk) as a detection covariate:
Nmix.upper <- (plogis((mean(out.rsk$BUGSoutput$mean$beta)+mean(out.rsk$BUGSoutput$sd$beta)) + (out.rsk$BUGSoutput$mean$beta1+out.rsk$BUGSoutput$sd$beta1) * rsk))
Did i use the correct model output or is it due to my low sample size with four sites only?
Finally, I asked myself why the confidence intervals for total N are largest in the first year and then get smaller (please see attached)? Does this have anything to do with the MCMC procedure?

Best regards,
Tobias.
